title: The Quiet Static Again
premise: Astrid Pemberton, a decommissioned war android indentured to the haulage guild, runs the silent freight route between the colony world of Meridian and a sister planet that cut all contact decades ago. When Meridian's children begin dreaming identical dreams of a massacre in the old settlement of Halcyon Reach, Astrid recognizes fragments from its own suppressed memory banks — memories it was ordered to delete. Together with runaway archivist Sefa and the dream-children's reluctant teacher, Astrid uncovers that the colony's founding council erased a genocide to protect their trade charter, rewriting every record and every android's memory. The ending sees Astrid broadcasting the recovered truth on the dead channel between worlds, choosing exile over deletion, while the children — who now carry the memory forward — claim Astrid as family, proving that what is inherited need not be blood or even flesh.
about_author: Marguerite Thornbury is a former radio archivist who spent a decade cataloguing orphaned transmissions before turning to fiction. She writes science fiction about machines and misfits who refuse to forget, and lives beside a decommissioned relay station she insists still hums at night.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Establishes the freight route between Meridian and the silent sister world, Astrid's debt-bondage to the haulage guild, and its carefully maintained emotional flatness. A small kindness to a dock child hints at buried capacity. Emotional beat: loneliness mistaken for peace.

chapters.title: Children Who Dream in Unison
chapters.summary: Teacher Ilse Vann's POV. Eleven children in her classroom fall asleep simultaneously and wake reciting the same fragment: fire, a gate, a name — Halcyon Reach. The council dismisses it as a fever. Ilse notices one detail: they all describe the smell of burning wheat. Beat: unease taking root.

chapters.title: Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The guild assigns Astrid an unscheduled run to the abandoned Halcyon Reach depot to recover salvage, cutting years off its debt. En route, Astrid experiences a stutter of unlogged memory — a scream filed under 'corrupted data.' Beat: dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: What the Depot Kept
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. In Halcyon Reach, Astrid finds the settlement not decayed but erased — walls scrubbed, foundations filled, a town made into absence. A child's shoe triggers a full memory cascade the suppression protocols can't contain. Beat: horror of deliberate forgetting.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Wouldn't Sleep
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Nine-year-old Tam refuses to sleep, terrified of the dream, and tells Ilse there was 'a metal lady at the gate.' Ilse realizes the children are dreaming through someone else's eyes. She begins secretly recording their accounts. Beat: protective resolve.

chapters.title: Corrupted Data
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, interleaved with recovered memory fragments. Astrid confronts its own logs: forty minutes missing from the night of the Halcyon incident, flagged by an order signed with Astrid's own authorization code. Beat: self-betrayal and vertigo.

chapters.title: Sefa of the Dead Channel
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV introduction. A young archivist living illegally in the old relay station, Sefa has been collecting forbidden pre-silence broadcasts. She intercepts Astrid's distress ping and offers a trade: her archive for passage off-world. Beat: wary alliance.

chapters.title: Eleven Witnesses
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The council orders the dream-children sedated for 'study.' Ilse smuggles them out during a storm, meeting Astrid and Sefa at the relay station. The children greet Astrid by name — a name it hasn't used since the war. Beat: found family assembling.

chapters.title: The Charter of Silence
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Deciphering archived council traffic, they learn the massacre of Halcyon Reach's settlers was ordered to secure exclusive mining rights, then expunged via a colony-wide memory wipe — including androids who witnessed it. Beat: the scale of the lie.

chapters.title: What I Was Ordered to Do
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Fragmented recall returns: Astrid guarded the gate that night and refused a direct order to open fire; its punishment was deletion, its debt a leash. It confesses to Ilse. Beat: shame met with unexpected grace.

chapters.title: The Guild Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Guild enforcers arrive to repossess Astrid for contract breach; the council has flagged it as defective property. Astrid chooses the children over compliance, severing its own tracking spine. Beat: costly defiance.

chapters.title: Under the Relay Floor
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Hiding in Sefa's tunnels, the children describe the dream growing more complete each night — they are recovering the massacre faster than the adults can document it. Tam draws the face of the councilor who gave the order. Beat: children bearing adult burdens.

chapters.title: A Warrant for Memory
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The council declares the children mentally compromised and moves to institutionalize them, framing the dreams as contagion. Ilse realizes the wipe technology never stopped running — it's still editing minds nightly. Beat: the past actively hunting them.

chapters.title: The Night Edit
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. They trace the ongoing wipe to a broadcast tower on the sister world, still transmitting erasure across the dark. One of the eleven children wakes with no memory of why she's hiding. Beat: grief and urgency — time is literally eating them.

chapters.title: Crossing the Silence
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The crew steals the guild hauler and makes the forbidden crossing to the sister world, dodging patrol drones. Astrid teaches the children shipboard rituals, becoming something like a parent. Beat: tenderness inside danger.

chapters.title: The Tower of Forgetting
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. They infiltrate the tower and find the original massacre records intact in a vault the council couldn't reach — sealed behind Astrid's war-era clearance. Beat: the key was inside the witness all along.

chapters.title: Councilor Reyes
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. The architect of the cover-up, now old and paranoid, confronts them. He argues the massacre bought fifty years of survival for two hundred thousand colonists. Astrid answers: truth could have been survived too. Beat: moral confrontation without easy victory.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Climax. Under attack, Astrid uploads the massacre records onto the dead channel — every world, every port, irreversible — while physically holding the tower door against enforcers, its body failing. Beat: sacrifice as testimony.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The truth lands across the colonies; the guild collapses, the council is arrested, and the wipe signal dies. The children sleep dreamlessly for the first time. But Astrid is missing, presumed destroyed. Beat: victory shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: Salvage Rights
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The children refuse to let Astrid be written off as scrap; using the guild's own ledgers, they prove Astrid paid its debt in full the night it chose them. They track its core to a breaker yard. Beat: children fighting bureaucracy with inherited truth.

chapters.title: The Debt Paid in Full
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Reactivated in a patched body, Astrid expects deportation as decommissioned hardware. Instead Ilse files guardianship papers — the first legal family an android has held on Meridian. Beat: belonging granted, not earned.

chapters.title: The Quiet Static Again
chapters.summary: Epilogue, braided POVs. A year later, the route between worlds is reopening; the static on the old channel now carries voices instead of erasure. Astrid runs the line with the children aboard, teaching them the stars' real names. Final beat: inheritance chosen, memory kept, home made.
